drivingQuestion: How does R' Yehuda account for a torn-open tumtum who fathered children?
outcomeNote: R' Yehuda's view survives: the paternity of the children is doubted

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: טוּמְטוּם וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְטוּמְטוּם דְּבֵירֵי, דְּאוֹתְבוּהּ אַבֵּי כּוּרְסְיָה וְאִיקְּרַע, וְאוֹלֵיד שְׁבַע בְּנִין! וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר לָךְ: חַזֵּר עַל בָּנָיו מֵאַיִן הֵם.
segments.en: § It is taught in the mishna that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» If «a tumtum,» whose external sexual organs are indeterminate, was torn open so that his genitals were exposed, and he was found to be a male, he must not perform ḥalitza because he is treated like a eunuch. «Rabbi Ami said: What» would «Rabbi Yehuda do with the tumtum» living in the town «of Biri, who was placed in a seat» for an operation, «and» the tissue covering his genitals «was torn» open «and» he later «fathered seven children?» Evidently, a tumtum who was torn open is not necessarily sexually impotent. The Gemara answers that «Rabbi Yehuda» could have «said to you:» Go and «inquire about his children» and find out «from where they came.» He did not believe that they were fathered by this man but rather by someone else.
